newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Wallenberg ended Sweden bank merge talks - magazine.
newsitem.headline: Wallenberg ended Sweden bank merge talks - magazine.

text.p: The head of Sweden's most powerful industrial family, Peter Wallenberg, said he was responsible for ending merger talks between commercial bank S-E-Banken and state-controlled Nordbanken.

In an interview with monthly business magazine Manadens Affarer, Wallenberg said he felt obliged to end the talks in February this year because of Finance Minister Erik Asbrink's political constraints.
"Sometimes a person has to take a step back," Wallenberg told Manadens Affarer.
"On one side of the negotiations was a businessman, myself, and on the other side sat a person who was interested in a deal but also had to take other factors into account.
"I was forced to respect this considering he was the country's finance minister and therefore subordinate to certain political constraints," Wallenberg told the magazine.
The state controls about 59 percent of Nordbanken.
S-E-Banken and Nordbanken, two of Sweden's four big banks, surprised the market in February by announcing merger talks between them had ended.
Rumours of a merger had fuelled Swedish banking shares since last autumn.

At the time no reason was given for the breakdown in talks by either the government or the Wallenbergs who hold 22 percent of S-E-Banken's votes and 21.2 percent of its capital, some through its investment company Investor AB.
But analysts suggested the potential job cuts could have been a reason. They estimated up to 4,000 jobs from a combined workforce of 16,000 could have been axed if the banks had merged.
The Swedish government is battling high unemployment -- running at 7.8 percent in May -- and has vowed to bring this figure down to around four percent by the year 2000.
Asbrink would probably have been reluctant to agree to sweeping job cuts, they said.
Disagreements about the state's ownership in the new bank was another reason suggested for the breakdown in talks.
Since the merger failed, the government has continued to express its intention of selling out of Nordbanken.
